userStories.title: Remove the dead failure categories and the tier-outcome pause path
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Remove ten dead FailureCategory members and make both exhausted-tier handlers retain only their existing failure path.

**Motivation** — Both callers of `handleNoTierAvailable` and `handleMaxAttemptsReached` (`execution/escalation/tier-escalation.ts:334`, `:350`) pass no category, so `resolveMaxAttemptsOutcome` (`escalation/max-attempts-outcome.ts`) always returns `"fail"` and both handlers' pause branches (`tier-outcome.ts:36-67`, `:106-137`) never run.

**Approach** — Part 1: failure categories and the tier-outcome pause path (US-001)

| Site | After |
|:---|:---|
| `execution/types.ts:10-50` `FailureCategory` | `"dependency-prep"` only, with its doc comment; the other ten members and the `isolation-violation` "dormant, not dead" comment go |
| `execution/escalation/max-attempts-outcome.ts` | deleted; `resolveMaxAttemptsOutcome` leaves `escalation/tier-escalation.ts:66`, `escalation/index.ts:14`, `execution/index.ts:12` and `execution/runner.ts:59` |
| `escalation/tier-outcome.ts:29-32`, `:99-102` | `handleNoTierAvailable(ctx)` and `handleMaxAttemptsReached(ctx)` lose the `failureCategory` parameter |
| `tier-outcome.ts:34-67`, `:104-137` | the `outcome` lookup and the pause branch go; each handler always marks the story failed, saves with `"failed"`, logs, appends progress and emits `story:failed` exactly as its fail branch does today, and passes `undefined` as the category to `markStoryFailed`; the `failureCategory` log field goes |
| `tier-outcome.ts:10`, `:17` | the `FailureCategory`, `markStoryPaused` and `verifyEscalationQuotes` imports go when nothing else in the file uses them |
| `prd/index.ts:311-335` `markStoryFailed` | unchanged: its optional `failureCategory?: FailureCategory` now admits only `"dependency-prep"`, which `iteration-runner.ts:160` still passes |

`prd.json` loading does not validate `failureCategory` (`prd/schema*.ts` has no rule for it), so a PRD saved by an older run with, for example, `"failureCategory": "verifier-rejected"` still loads and keeps the string.

**Interface** — `handleNoTierAvailable(ctx)` and `handleMaxAttemptsReached(ctx)` lose the `failureCategory` parameter. Keep their EscalationHandlerResult contract and the optional `failureCategory?: FailureCategory` on `markStoryFailed`. Do not clear a previously recorded category as an incidental change; absence pins use a story with no existing category.

**Scope** — In: the registry, deleted resolver module/re-exports, both handlers, their affected fixtures/tests, unused imports and associated ratchet reductions. Out: post-run/metrics (US-002), session roles (US-003), prompt roles (US-004), config guard/stages (US-005/US-006). Keep dependency-prep, markStoryFailed's optional category, UserStory.failureCategory and WorktreeDependencyPreparationError.failureCategory.
- Out: Removing the `dependency-prep` failure category, the `failureCategory` parameter of `markStoryFailed`, or `UserStory.failureCategory`: `iteration-runner.ts:160` still writes it.
- Out: Removing the `failureCategory` field of `WorktreeDependencyPreparationError` (`worktree/types.ts:22`), which nothing reads: it belongs to issue #2823 (declarations unreachable for reasons other than the pipeline).

**Implementation and test updates** — In test/unit/execution/escalation/tier-outcome.test.ts delete the two pause-reason persistence describes and the cost source on story:paused describe; delete both paused-progress tests and the fallback-totalCost story:paused test. Rename both fail-category tests to `marks the story failed (not paused)` and remove category arguments from every retained call. In tier-outcome-progress.test.ts delete the two pause tests and drop undefined arguments from the fail tests. In test/unit/execution/story-failure-spend.test.ts drop all three handler category arguments; convert `story:paused reports total spend too` to `story:failed reports total spend for a story with no tier left` asserting the same spend on story:failed, and remove its resolver comment. Delete resolver-only describes/imports from tier-escalation.test.ts, tier-escalation-greenfield.test.ts and test/integration/execution/runner-escalation.test.ts; keep the greenfield file's #1575, #1710, #1745 and #1761 describes. Other integration tests passing removed categories are deleted. In test/unit/prd/prd-failure-category.test.ts use dependency-prep for retained writer tests; remove member-only enumeration tests and retain absence, unknown-story and passed-to-failed-reset behavior. Extend those existing tests with the loadPRD historical-input pin, without registry validation or casts that restore removed members. Both handlers always return outcome failed; retain reason strings, progress, savePrdProgress and total/error spend semantics.

**Verification** — Run these steps in `packages/nax` under the session's gate policy.
1. `bun run typecheck`. A removed union member, field, parameter or export that is still referenced fails here.
2. A string sweep. For each registry value the story removes, `rg -n --fixed-strings '"<value>"' src bin scripts`, and for each function, constant, type and file it removes, `rg -n -w '<name>' src bin test scripts`. Expected: only the remaining hits the story lists, else stop. A hit in code is a missed reference. A hit in a comment is a stale comment and is reworded, in any file (a comment edit needs no Modifies entry). Line numbers in Design and `### Modifies` are at `dfcbc053a`; a story that runs after another story edited the same file locates each site by its symbol or test name. Sweep values: `"isolation-violation"`, `"session-failure"`, `"tests-failing"`, `"test-incorrect"`, `"full-suite-gate-exhausted"`, `"verifier-rejected"`, `"greenfield-no-tests"`, `"no-tests-authored"`, `"review-incomplete"`, `"runtime-crash"`; names `resolveMaxAttemptsOutcome`, `max-attempts-outcome`. Expected remaining hits: none in `src`, `bin` or `scripts` (the `"runtime-crash"` strings in `packages/nax-agent` are the separate `AdapterFailure` registry and are outside the swept paths). Delete resolver references in tests as well; deliberate historical category test inputs stay.
3. `bun run check:complexity:update`, and `bun run check:file-sizes -- --update-baseline` when that check reports a lowerable entry. After `check:all` is green, `bun run check:test-escape-hatches:update` lowers the escape-hatch totals the deleted tests carried.
4. `bun run check:all` and `bun run test`.
A trimmed source file also drops the imports only its removed code used; biome's `noUnusedImports` reports them. Regenerate scripts/baselines/complexity-baseline.json and lower scripts/baselines/test-escape-hatches-baseline.json for deleted/shrunk code only. AC4 and AC5 are retention pins that may pass before removal.

userStories.title: Remove the dead post-run phases and metrics sources
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Narrow post-run event/TUI state to review and metrics/curator source handling to the two produced source values.

**Motivation** — The TUI keeps state and rows for `acceptance`, `acceptance-setup`, `regression` and `finish` (`tui/hooks/usePipelineBusEvents.ts:70-75`, `tui/components/StoriesPanel.tsx:184-191`, `tui/App.tsx:115-122`) that are never set.

**Approach** — Part 2: post-run phases and metrics sources (US-002)

| Site | After |
|:---|:---|
| `pipeline/event-bus/index.ts:204` `PostRunPhase` | `"review"` |
| `tui/hooks/usePipelineBusEvents.ts:69-75` `postRunPhases` | `{ review?: PostRunPhaseState }`, its doc comment says "Post-run phase status (review)"; the two `postrun:phase:*` handlers (`:245-261`) are unchanged |
| `tui/components/StoriesPanel.tsx:23-28` `StoriesPanelProps.postRunPhases` | `{ review?: PostRunPhaseState }`, with its comment trimmed to match |
| `tui/components/StoriesPanel.tsx:184-192` | the section renders when `postRunPhases.review` is set and holds only the review row; the acceptance and regression rows go |
| `tui/App.tsx:115-122` `runningPostRunPhase` | `"post-run: review"` when the review phase is running, else `undefined` |
| `metrics/types.ts:169-170` `StoryMetrics.source` | `"completion-phase" | "execution-failed"`, with the doc comment trimmed to those two |
| `metrics/types.ts:182-183` `rectificationCost` | deleted with its doc comment |
| `plugins/builtin/curator/collect.ts:48-58` `verdictSource` | returns `"completion-phase"` or `"execution-failed"` when the row carries one, else `"execution"` |
| `plugins/builtin/curator/types.ts:181` `VerdictObservation.payload.source` | `"execution" | "completion-phase" | "execution-failed"` |

An older `metrics.json` row whose `source` is `parallel`, `sequential` or `rectification` now reaches the curator as `"execution"`, the existing fallback for an unknown value.

**Interface** — `PostRunPhase` is `"review"`; post-run state is `{ review?: PostRunPhaseState }`; `StoryMetrics.source` is `"completion-phase" | "execution-failed"`; `VerdictObservation.payload.source` is `"execution" | "completion-phase" | "execution-failed"`. Preserve event handler and artifact-reader entry points.

**Scope** — In: the post-run registry, hook/props/App presentation, metrics field deletion and curator normalization/types, affected tests and ratchet reductions. Out: failure categories (US-001), session registry (US-003), prompt roles (US-004), permission/MCP guards and stages (US-005/US-006). Keep status.json post-run state, PRE_RUN_STAGES, pre-run rows, rules stages, plugin PhaseDetails/RunPhaseDetails and historical failingTestFiles. Do not rewrite or reject old metrics rows.

Extend packages/nax/test/unit/plugins/builtin/curator-collector-metrics.test.ts for completion-phase preservation and historical rectification fallback through collectObservations; use matching runId artifacts, not private-function or source-content checks. Keep non-compact review row/empty heading behavior. Reword the LiveActivityPanel post-run example only.

**Verification** — Run these steps in `packages/nax` under the session's gate policy.
1. `bun run typecheck`. A removed union member, field, parameter or export that is still referenced fails here.
2. A string sweep. For each registry value the story removes, `rg -n --fixed-strings '"<value>"' src bin scripts`, and for each function, constant, type and file it removes, `rg -n -w '<name>' src bin test scripts`. Expected: only the remaining hits the story lists, else stop. A hit in code is a missed reference. For `"parallel"` and `"sequential"`: any hit outside `metrics/` and `plugins/builtin/curator/` is a different vocabulary (run mode, plan strategy) and is listed, not changed. userStories.title: Remove the dead session roles
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Remove fourteen dead canonical session roles and their reviewer-guard/tool-capability entries while retaining old artifact readability.

**Motivation** — `REVIEWER_SESSION_ROLES` (`review/reviewer-guard/guard.ts:14-22`) and `REQUIRED_TOOLS_BY_ROLE` (`scripts/check-op-tool-capability.ts:46-73`) are typed as plain strings, so their dead entries are not even compile-checked.

**Approach** — Part 3: session roles (US-003)

| Site | After |
|:---|:---|
| `runtime/session-role.ts:14-86` | the union and `KNOWN_SESSION_ROLES` drop the 14 roles in Motivation; the remaining 16, in this order: `main`, `implementer`, `reviewer-semantic`, `reviewer-adversarial`, `reviewer-fix`, `plan`, `plan-refine`, `auto`, `setup`, `advisor`, `wf-implementer`, `wf-story-review`, `wf-rereview`, `wf-branch-review`, `wf-branch-fix`, `wf-repair` |
| `review/reviewer-guard/guard.ts:14-22` `REVIEWER_SESSION_ROLES` | drops `finish-review-spec` and `finish-review-quality` |
| `scripts/check-op-tool-capability.ts:46-73` `REQUIRED_TOOLS_BY_ROLE` | keeps `implementer`, `plan`, `plan-refine`; drops `test-writer`, `source-fix`, `test-fix`, `repo-scoped-test-fix`, `fix-gen`, `finish-fix`, `verifier`, `acceptance-gen`, with the comments that describe only them (the #1936 note, the verifier doc block, and the doc line "`verifier` never edits"); both occurrences of "three roles" in the comments ("the three roles below", "These three roles never edit") become "these roles" |

`reviewer-semantic`, `reviewer-adversarial` and `reviewer-fix` also have no producer, but they stay in this wave: `runtime/middleware/review-audit.ts:11-17` maps exactly those three to the review audit's reviewer kind, and no workflow role maps to it, so deleting them decides whether workflow reviewers are audited. That decision is Out of Scope. `deriveSessionRole` (`runtime/usage-auditor.ts:81-86`) matches a session name's trailing role over `KNOWN_SESSION_ROLES`; live session names never end in a removed role, and rows already written keep the `sessionRole` they recorded. `knownSessionRole` (`runtime/session-role.ts:99`) returns `undefined` for a removed role, as for any unknown string. When a resumed ACP session header names such a role, the caller at `agents/manager.ts:507` falls back to the caller's role or `"main"`; that existing fallback belongs to the manager, not to `knownSessionRole` itself.

**Interface** — Remove precisely `test-writer`, `verifier`, `diagnose`, `source-fix`, `test-fix`, `repo-scoped-test-fix`, `acceptance-gen`, `refine`, `fix-gen`, `finish-review-spec`, `finish-review-quality`, `finish-fix`, `nbf-worth-check` and `decompose` from CanonicalSessionRole and KNOWN_SESSION_ROLES. Keep the existing isSessionRole, knownSessionRole, deriveSessionRole, ReviewerTreeGuard and queryCostLedger entry points. `knownSessionRole` itself returns undefined for an unknown role; the caller at agents/manager.ts supplies the caller-role/main fallback.

**Scope** — In: the canonical role registry, two removed guard memberships, eight removed capability rows, stale role comments and affected fixtures/ratchets. Out: FailureCategory and outcomes (US-001), PostRunPhase/metrics (US-002), prompt guardrail/isolation roles (US-004), permission/MCP stages (US-005/US-006). Keep reviewer-semantic/adversarial/fix audit mappings, config override/session-tier/CLI vocabularies, scratch readers, plugin payload families and old ledger/audit/token rows. Do not broaden or redesign tool policies or reviewer auditing.
- Out: Removing the session roles `reviewer-semantic`, `reviewer-adversarial` and `reviewer-fix`, or changing `reviewerFromRole` in `runtime/middleware/review-audit.ts`: no workflow role reaches the review audit's dispatch recording today, and whether it should is a follow-up decision, not a deletion.
- Out: Removing the scratch kinds `tdd-session` and `self-verification` or their role fields in `session/scratch-writer.ts`: their readers (`context/engine/providers/session-scratch.ts`, `context/engine/handlers/query-scratch.ts`) render entries persisted by older runs, the same reason B3a kept `StoryMetrics.failingTestFiles`.

In test/unit/review/reviewer-guard/guard.test.ts retitle the seven-role closed-world test as `the role set is the five reviewer roles`, asserting reviewer-semantic, reviewer-adversarial, wf-story-review, wf-rereview, wf-branch-review; drive former finish-review beforeTurn/afterTurn and concurrency cases with wf-branch-review/wf-story-review. SessionDescriptor.role is typed as SessionRole (src/session/types.ts:69-73), not an opaque string. For the intentional old-role negative pin, construct the normal descriptor with the existing desc helper, then use Object.assign on that test fixture to inject the historical runtime role before calling beforeTurn. This follows the cast-free fixture technique documented in .nax/rules/test-ratchets.md; do not widen the production descriptor, restore a removed role, add a helper or introduce a cast/suppression. The opaque string boundary is SessionHandle.role, not SessionDescriptor.role. In test/unit/scripts/check-op-tool-capability.test.ts delete verifier/fix-role requirement tests, iterate implementer only for Write/Edit and plan/plan-refine for Write-only. Replace `a fix-role op missing RunCommand is a violation` with `an implementer op missing Edit is a violation`: role implementer, tools [Read, Write], missing [Edit]. In test/integration/tdd/audit-naming.test.ts use implementer/wf-implementer; in test/integration/acceptance/audit-naming.test.ts use a live role; delete tests existing only to name a removed role. 2. A string sweep. Expected: only the remaining hits the story lists, else stop. A hit in code is a missed reference. A hit in a comment is a stale comment and is reworded, in any file (a comment edit needs no Modifies entry). Line numbers in Design and `### Modifies` are at `dfcbc053a`; a story that runs after another story edited the same file locates each site by its symbol or test name. userStories.title: Warn about and strip removed stage names at config load
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Introduce immutable warned-and-stripped compatibility handling for removed MCP/permission stage names at all three existing loader strip sites, before US-006 contracts the enums.

**Motivation** — No op declares the `rectification`, `regression` or `acceptance` stage; the last ones went in B2a and B2b-3.

**Approach** — Part 5: the removed-stage config guard (US-005)

A new module `src/config/removed-stage-names.ts` (`config-guards.ts` is at 592 of its 600 allowed lines, and `loader.ts` at 591):

**Interface**
```typescript
/** Stage names no operation runs in since pipeline mode was removed. */
export const REMOVED_STAGE_NAMES: readonly string[] = ["rectification", "regression", "acceptance"];

const REMOVED_STAGE_HINT = "no nax operation runs in this stage since pipeline mode was removed";

/** Drop removed stage names from mcp.servers.<id>.stages and drop un-inherited
 *  execution.permissions.<removed> blocks, warning once per dropped item.
 *  Returns a new object; never mutates `conf`. */
export function stripRemovedStageNames(
  conf: Record<string, unknown>,
  warn?: (msg: string) => void,
): Record<string, unknown>;

/** stripRemovedNoOpKeys, then stripRemovedStageNames, with one sink. */
export function stripRemovedConfig(
  conf: Record<string, unknown>,
  warn?: (msg: string) => void,
): Record<string, unknown>;
```

- For each `mcp.servers.<id>` object whose `stages` is an array, every element equal to a removed name is dropped, and `warn` receives `Config value "<name>" in mcp.servers.<id>.stages has been removed — <hint>. Remove it from your config.` once per dropped element. A server whose stages become `[]` stays: an empty list attaches the server to no stage (`providerAttachesTo`, `nax-agent/src/tools/provider-types.ts:78-80`), the same as a removed stage did.
- For each removed name `<name>` that is a key of `execution.permissions`, if no other block under `execution.permissions` has `inherit === "<name>"`, the key is dropped and `warn` receives `Config key "execution.permissions.<name>" has been removed — <hint>. Remove it from your config.` Otherwise the block stays and nothing is warned. "Inherited" is judged against the input object, before any block is dropped: with `rectification: { inherit: "regression" }` and `regression: { ... }` and nothing inheriting `rectification`, `rectification` is dropped and `regression` stays. A sibling value that is `null` or not an object names no inherit target and is skipped by the scan.
- Missing or non-object `mcp`, `mcp.servers`, a server, `execution` or `execution.permissions`, and a non-array `stages`, are left as they are, with no warning.
- `loader.ts` imports `stripRemovedConfig` in place of `stripRemovedNoOpKeys` and calls it at each of the three sites that call `stripRemovedNoOpKeys` today (`:256`, `:532`, `:567`), with the same sink each passes now. The strip runs after `validatePermissionsBlock` (`loader.ts:250`), so an `inherit` that names a dropped block cannot occur. The `:567` site strips the per-package result after the package profile layers are applied (`applyPackageProfileLayers`, `loader.ts:545`) and before `NaxConfigSchema.safeParse` at `:573`. A package overlay file's own top-level `mcp` block never reaches it (`mergePackageConfig`, `config/merge.ts:72-100`, merges only agent, models, routing, execution, review, acceptance, quality, context and project), but a package profile (`<package>/.nax/profiles/<name>.json`, named by the overlay's `profile`) deep-merges any key, `mcp` included.

**Scope** — In: create src/config/removed-stage-names.ts and test/unit/config/removed-stage-names.test.ts; replace the loader import/three strip calls while preserving their warning sinks, validation order and existing no-op key handling. Out: registry contraction and inert-Bash stage deletion (US-006); failure categories, post-run/metrics, session roles and prompt roles (US-001 through US-004). The registries keep their members in this story; US-006 removes them. No warning-count assertion for a value reaching both root/package strips; warnDedupe owns that unchanged. No repository .nax files are modified by implementation; .nax test fixture paths are under temporary projects only.
- Out: US-005 only: asserting how many times a warning is emitted when the same removed value reaches both the root strip and a package-merge strip (`loader.ts:532`, `:567`): the existing per-resolution dedupe (`warnDedupe`) owns that, unchanged by this wave.
- Out: Updating `docs/`, config field descriptions or release notes for the removed stages: wave B4.
- Out: Editing the repository's own `.nax/config.json`, `.nax/rules/` or any file under `.nax/`: read-only to the run.

**Implementation and test updates** — Mirror stripRemovedNoOpKeys' reconstruction/ownership pattern without copying its near-limit module or mutating any nested object. Treat JSON records defensively, including null/scalar siblings; preserve unknown/invalid nonremoved values for the existing schema to diagnose. Compute inheritance against the input, not an incrementally stripped result; do not transitively remove now-unused templates. stripRemovedConfig calls stripRemovedNoOpKeys and then stripRemovedStageNames with the same optional sink. At the root use defaultConfigWarn, at both package sites keep warnDedupe.warn. Unit tests go in the new test file, and loadConfig/loadConfigForWorkdir seam tests also go there as specified, using the existing strip-removed-noop-keys.test.ts temp-project, cache reset and logger/addSink pattern. Root AC8/AC9 enter above the root strip; package AC10 uses overlay profile p plus packages/app/.nax/profiles/p.json, because a plain package overlay mcp block is not merged. Assert resolved values, not source text or helper-only behavior. In the same new seam-test file, exercise the Failure Handling permission-block cases through loadConfig: an un-inherited removed block resolves absent with its warning, while a removed block inherited by review resolves retained without a removed-stage warning. Capture matching messages via the existing logger sink and keep unrelated config warnings out of these assertions. Preserve existing no-op-key loader tests. The guard is prerequisite behavior, not a schema relaxation: unknown stages remain errors once existing schemas run.

**Verification** — Run these steps in `packages/nax` under the session's gate policy.

2. A string sweep. For each registry value the story removes, `rg -n --fixed-strings '"<value>"' src bin scripts`, and for each function, constant, type and file it removes, `rg -n -w '<name>' src bin test scripts`. Expected: only the remaining hits the story lists, else stop. A hit in code is a missed reference. A hit in a comment is a stale comment and is reworded, in any file (a comment edit needs no Modifies entry). This story removes no registry member/function/constant/type/file, so the deletion sweep has no targets.
